proof_summary: Couple the evolutions from initial masses \(n\) and \(n+1\): their difference remains a single “defect” unit, which moves one cell right exactly when the underlying cell has odd mass. A contiguity-and-mass invariant forces this defect to be at \(n-2\) or \(n-1\) when the \(n\)-process stabilizes; on the all-ones stable background it then moves right once per step, so the larger process stabilizes two or one steps later, respectively.
